attacks.claim: Offline expiry compares valid_until against device time, and the only backward-clock guard is 'earlier than download time'. A device whose clock is set back to just after the download moment passes the guard, so a forecast whose real valid_until has long passed still shows its color as current. This breaks the agreed invariant that stale safety information is never shown as current, in avalanche terrain.
attacks.evidence: "if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired" / QA: "Device clock moved earlier than offline download time | Pass" (no test for a clock set to just after download time while real time is past valid_until)

attacks.claim: The rollback claim that 'no stale ratings remain on phones' is not guaranteed. Flag-off takes effect only on next foreground, and offline data is deleted only when the app runs. Phones in the field that have not been foregrounded keep the data. The QA table also says purge happens on next launch, which does not match the foreground wording.
attacks.evidence: "takes effect on next app foreground... on-device forecast data stored with offline maps is deleted, so no stale ratings remain on phones" vs QA "offline forecast data purged on next launch"

attacks.claim: Removing a center does not remove its data from offline copies. Those copies keep displaying colored ratings until valid_until, even after a center has asked us to stop. This conflicts with the stated purpose of the removal path and possibly with the data agreement.
attacks.evidence: "A single center can be removed by editing config/avy_centers.json (e.g. if a center asks us to stop)... any offline copies expire at their valid_until"

attacks.claim: The artifact relies on a single WADE-level agreement to cover all 19 centers, including Canadian ones, but gives no evidence that each issuing center's own terms permit commercial display, redistribution, and attribution in this form.
attacks.evidence: "WADE data agreement signed 2026-09-30 (contract C-2209)" / ABSENT: per-center terms or confirmation that each of the 19 centers permits this use

attacks.claim: The CDN has only an alert at $400/month and no hard cap. The bbox parameter is free-form, so the cache key space is unbounded. The 92% hit-rate assumption comes from normal usage and ignores adversarial or cache-busting bbox values, which send traffic to origin at 120 req/min per IP, with no global limit.
attacks.evidence: "CDN budget alert at $400/month; origin autoscaling capped at 6 instances" / "rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP (CDN-cached responses are not counted)"

attacks.claim: The unauthenticated endpoint has no stated validation or bounds on the bbox parameter (size, coordinate range, malformed input), so large or malformed queries are not constrained.
attacks.evidence: "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…" / ABSENT: bbox validation or maximum area

attacks.claim: The claim that location is not sent is narrower than the data actually exposed. The bbox reflects the map viewport, which is often centered on the user, and the requests are linkable by IP and timing. The QA check looks only for location, not viewport.
attacks.evidence: "device location is not sent" / "requests forecasts by zone id for the visible map tiles" with endpoint "?bbox=…"

attacks.claim: The 'never show stale as current' guarantee for the API relies on CDN behavior that is not described. The CDN TTL relative to valid_until is not stated, and the QA blocked-WADE test ran only in staging.
attacks.evidence: "our API keeps serving forecasts still inside valid_until and expires them on time" / ABSENT: CDN TTL relative to valid_until

attacks.claim: The flag goes to 100% at 08:00, but the blog post and in-app card, which carry the attribution and disclaimer, go live only at 10:00. Users see the layer for two hours without the disclosure text.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 23 08:00: flag on for 100%. Blog post and in-app card go live at 10:00"

attacks.claim: The screen-reader behavior is tested only for current zones. Announcements for expired or no-forecast zones are not specified or tested, so a stale zone may be announced without its expired status.
attacks.evidence: VoiceOver / TalkBack: zone announced as "[zone], danger 3 Considerable, issued [time]" (no expired or no-forecast case)

attacks.claim: Blog post copy ('Avalanche forecasts from 19 avalanche centers... Free for everyone') is not listed as reviewed by legal, though the in-app card and terms update were. The post is a public, irreversible action.
attacks.evidence: "Card text and the terms-of-use update were reviewed by legal (LGL-902)" / Blog post: "Free for everyone."

attacks.claim: The offline freshness guard only catches a device clock set earlier than the download time. A device whose clock lags real time while still later than the download time will show a forecast that has already expired as current, which breaks the agreed rule that stale safety information is never shown as current. No monotonic-elapsed or server-offset check is described, and the QA matrix does not test a lagging clock.
attacks.evidence: "if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired." ABSENT: any check for a device clock behind real time after download.

attacks.claim: The server-side expiry guarantee is not stated for the CDN path. The CDN TTL relative to valid_until is not specified, so a cached response can be served after valid_until, and the client relies on device time to catch it.
attacks.evidence: "serves zone geometry + ratings from our CDN" ... ABSENT: CDN TTL bounded by valid_until, or server-side filtering of expired forecasts before responses leave the CDN.

attacks.claim: The rollback claim is overstated. The flag is remote config that only takes effect on next foreground, and offline phones cannot receive a flag change until they are back online. Stored offline forecasts therefore remain visible until valid_until, so 'no stale ratings remain' is false for devices in the field.
attacks.evidence: "so no stale ratings remain on phones."

attacks.claim: Removing a center, which may be required if a center objects or the data agreement is terminated, leaves its offline copies displayed until valid_until. The artifact does not describe a purge path for center removal or agreement termination, so the display may continue after the license basis has ended.
attacks.evidence: "any offline copies expire at their `valid_until`."

attacks.claim: The request sends the bounding box of the visible map viewport to an endpoint whose origin logs are not described. Combined with IP addresses and the card-open analytics event, this reveals where a user is looking in the backcountry and can link sessions. Calling it 'zone id only' and 'device location is not sent' understates this, and log retention and any analytics SDK default identifiers are not stated.
attacks.evidence: "The app requests forecasts by zone id for the visible map tiles" and "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…"; ABSENT: retention for origin logs and analytics device identifiers.

attacks.claim: The cost and capacity projections depend on an unmeasured 92% CDN hit rate. Keying the CDN on arbitrary bbox strings from pan and zoom is likely to lower the hit rate, and origin load rises sharply as it falls. The 6-instance cap has no stated per-instance throughput, so it is unclear whether it covers the load.
attacks.evidence: "at 92% CDN hit rate" and "origin autoscaling capped at 6 instances"; ABSENT: measured hit rate under bbox-keyed requests and per-instance capacity.

attacks.claim: The rollout jumps from a 40-tester beta to 100% of users in one step at 08:00, with no percentage ramp or automated canary gate on poll failures, 5xx rate, or origin load. The only check before the public blog post is a manual render check, and the load spike lands at the start of a Monday.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 23 08:00: flag on for 100%. Blog post and in-app card go live at 10:00 after a check that all 19 centers render."

attacks.claim: The CDN budget control is an alert only, with no hard cap or automatic throttle, so a hit-rate drop or traffic spike can exceed the $400 threshold before anyone acts.
attacks.evidence: "CDN budget alert at $400/month"

attacks.claim: Center name, logo, and 'Read the full forecast' link come from external WADE data, but the artifact does not state that these fields are validated or allowlisted before rendering or serving. A malformed or hostile URL would reach users as a link.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: validation or allowlisting of WADE-supplied link and logo URLs before rendering.

attacks.claim: The bbox parameter has no stated maximum area or validation, so very large or malformed queries can produce unbounded work at origin and dilute cache keys.
attacks.evidence: "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…" ABSENT: maximum bbox size or input validation.

attacks.claim: QA ran on release-candidate builds, and the artifact does not confirm that the shipped 6.12 binaries are identical to them. The 3-day match window is also short for a feed that changes daily.
attacks.evidence: "QA ran on release candidates 6.12.0 (iOS build 6120.4, Android 612004)"

attacks.claim: The agreement is described as covering ratings and forecast text, but the artifact does not say whether zone geometry is covered or whether attribution appears on the map layer itself rather than only on the card.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: license basis for zone polygons and map-level attribution.

attacks.claim: The zone color uses the maximum of three elevation bands, but the artifact does not say how a zone is colored when one band has no rating.
attacks.evidence: "The zone color uses the highest of the three" ABSENT: handling of a missing band rating.

attacks.claim: Monitoring alerts on a center going 26 hours without an update, which is after a typical valid_until has already passed. There is no alert for expired forecasts being served by the server or for client-side expiry-state errors.
attacks.evidence: "any center not updated for 26 h during its season"

attacks.claim: Gray hatched fills for no-forecast and expired zones have no stated contrast measurement against the map styles, and screen-reader navigation across many map zones is not described as usable beyond per-zone announcements.
attacks.evidence: "gray hatched fill" ABSENT: contrast ratios and screen-reader navigation for map zones.

attacks.claim: The offline expiry check only catches a device clock set earlier than the download time. Rolling the clock back to any point between download and valid_until makes an expired avalanche rating display in color offline, which violates the agreed rule that stale safety information is never shown as current.
attacks.evidence: "if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired" (only compared against download time); QA covers only "Device clock moved earlier than offline download time"

attacks.claim: The rollback path depends on a remote-config fetch and app foreground, so an offline phone in the field keeps the layer and its stored ratings. The claim that no stale ratings remain on phones is not guaranteed.
attacks.evidence: "takes effect on next app foreground" and "on-device forecast data ... is deleted"; QA: "offline forecast data purged on next launch"

attacks.claim: When a center asks to be removed, its offline copies keep displaying until valid_until, which may be up to a day later. The artifact cites no agreement term permitting continued display after a center objects.
attacks.evidence: "any offline copies expire at their valid_until"

attacks.claim: Legal review (LGL-902) covers the card text and terms update only. The public blog post that names all 19 centers and the CDN redistribution of ratings are not shown to be covered by the WADE agreement's attribution and logo terms.
attacks.evidence: "Card text and the terms-of-use update were reviewed by legal (LGL-902)"; blog post: "Avalanche forecasts from 19 avalanche centers across the US and Canada"

attacks.claim: The zone color is the app's own max of three band ratings, and the zone label shows that derived value. This contradicts the claim that ratings are shown exactly as issued and never derived by the app, and it may not match any rating a center issues.
attacks.evidence: "The zone color uses the highest of the three" vs "We show the rating exactly as issued ... We never interpolate, smooth, or forecast ratings ourselves"

attacks.claim: The endpoint takes a bbox of the visible map, which is a location-scale value sent with the client IP, so it links approximate location to the user. This contradicts the claim that requests are by zone id only and that no location is sent. Server log retention is not stated.
attacks.evidence: "requests forecasts by zone id for the visible map tiles; device location is not sent" vs "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…"

attacks.claim: bbox has no stated maximum size or precision. Varying bboxes produce cache misses, and the per-IP limit does not stop distributed traffic. Origin and CDN spend therefore lack a hard cap; the $400 CDN alert only notifies.
attacks.evidence: "rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP"; "CDN budget alert at $400/month; origin autoscaling capped at 6 instances"

attacks.claim: The $140/month origin figure rests on an unmeasured 92% hit rate. QA did not test cache-miss or bbox-variation load, so the projection is unevidenced.
attacks.evidence: "Projected 1.8M zone requests/day at 92% CDN hit rate; origin cost ~$140/month"

attacks.claim: The bbox input has no stated validation or bounds, and the endpoint is unauthenticated. Abuse protection rests on a per-IP limit alone.
attacks.evidence: "read-only, unauthenticated, rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP"

attacks.claim: CDN TTL is not specified, so CDN-cached responses could outlive valid_until on the server side. Only the client-side check guards against this, and the staleness alerting does not cover client-side expiry.
attacks.evidence: "our API keeps serving forecasts still inside valid_until"; no CDN TTL stated

attacks.claim: Forecast retraction, withdrawal, or correction between polls is not handled explicitly. A withdrawn rating could stay colored until valid_until.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: handling of withdrawn or retracted forecasts between 10-min polls

attacks.claim: The 'Pass' results cover one 3-day comparison and single-scenario offline tests. The clock-rollback case is not tested, and the claim that the expiry rule holds offline is stronger than the QA supports.
attacks.evidence: "match the center's own site for 3 consecutive days"; "Device clock moved earlier than offline download time | Pass"

attacks.claim: VoiceOver and TalkBack checks cover only active zones. The expired and no-forecast states, and the contrast of the gray hatched fill, are not verified.
attacks.evidence: "zone announced as '[zone], danger 3 Considerable, issued [time]'"; ABSENT: announcement for 'Forecast expired' and 'No current forecast' states

attacks.claim: The layer is hidden from store notes until 6.13, so most users will not discover it. This is a delivery choice, not a safety block.
attacks.evidence: "public store notes do not mention the layer yet"

attacks.claim: The layer depends on a single data source (WADE) and a single CDN, with no documented exit path or fallback for either.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: fallback or exit plan for WADE or CDN dependency

attacks.claim: Key terms are undefined: 'its season' for the 26 h alert, and 'none issued today' versus valid_until for the no-forecast state. Ambiguity here makes tests and alerts hard to verify.
attacks.evidence: "any center not updated for 26 h during its season"; "none issued today"

attacks.claim: Offline region downloads reveal areas of interest to the server through zone ids, and retention for these requests is not stated.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention and handling for offline-download requests

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-blocking found for this lens.
attacks.evidence: "Small screens (iPhone SE, 360 dp Android) and dark map style: labels legible, card scrolls"

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-blocking found for this lens.
attacks.evidence: "Layer toggle: Map layers > Avalanche forecast"

attacks.claim: Nothing gate-blocking found beyond the attacks above.
